sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Motion Picture International Copyright Distribution and Licensing

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic legal tradition with Germanic influences)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg has concluded more than 80 bilateral investment treaties (BITs) with third countries including France, Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands, and the United States
The Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) provides free establishment and capital movement protections applicable to EU/EEA counterparties

The Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (MAAC) and the OECD Model-based double taxation agreements (DTAAs) with a full active network of 54+ treaty jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML/CFT Law), consolidated version; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 March 2021 concerning the Register of Beneficial Owners; Law of 25 March 2020 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended) for SCSp formation; Law of 12 March 2004 on the organization of the notarial profession

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each beneficial owner and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent public authority in jurisdiction of residence (acting on notarially certified copies)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (certificat d'existence) for any corporate participant other than the initial limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original registry of incorporation of the corporate participant

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for the forming limited partner to appoint the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary or recognized foreign notary with competent legal authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration form (autorité administrative/AML) identifying the ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) / Luxembourg Business Registers

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all beneficial owners, general partners, and appointed managers against Luxembourg domestic politically exposed person (PEP) lists, EU anti-money laundering directives, OFAC and UN sanction lists, and EU consolidated financial sanctions list; enhanced forced-match due diligence for materially sensitive film-licensing counterparties with East-Asia/emerging market nexus, including required risk rating and documentary proof of beneficial ownership chain in the formation file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Statutory registration and publication must be conducted in French or optionally in German; names are transliterated to Latin script only; use of Luxembourg language (luxembourgish) is permitted but must be paired with a French or German transliteration; acronyms restricted by notary approval and public order.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: File a written contestation addressed to the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) within one month of the rejection notice, enclosing the negative certificate and legal arguments for distinctiveness; if rejected, submit to the relevant Luxembourg Ministry (usually the Minister of Justice) a parallel administrative appeal; final judicial relief is available before the Tribunal Administratif within three months of the expiry of the administrative deadline. The 30-day reservation may be extended once for another 30-day window upon written request and payment of extension fees if the delay is due to document legalization.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for an SCSp under Luxembourg commercial law if a registered office is in the Grand Duchy and the evergreen administrative seat is maintained; however, for a film licensing undertaking as a pure copyright distribution vehicle, the authorities may require adequate substance in Luxembourg to avoid tax reporting overflow into other jurisdictions; a physical or co-working office is not strictly mandatory at incorporation but practical for commercial substance and compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low – approximately 5% to 10% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by tax authorities or AML/CFT supervisors; more likely in the presence of non-resident material management or high-risk counterparties; formal documentary checks are more frequent than unannounced site visits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance negative certificate and distinct-name verification at Luxembourg Business Registers
Notarial deed drafting, execution and apostille certification of the SCSp partnership agreement
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial fee prescribed by Luxembourg Law of 3 December 1982

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO registration filing and beneficial-owner certificate with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official tariff under Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 March 2021

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization bundle for foreign corporate and passport documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / competent foreign issuing authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille Convention fixed fees plus prevailing consular translation service

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal due diligence opinion on UBO chain, PEP/sanctions screening and name adverse-text analysis
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg law firm / AML compliance counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark hourly rates for pre-incorporation work (EUR 250 per hour; 8-10 hour scope)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office initial annual seat fee at a Luxembourg administrative-services provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a standard SCSp registered office arrangement

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 936-951 introducing the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp) (reformed by Law of 23 March 2016 and subsequent amendments); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 March 2016 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / Partnership Agreement (Contrat de société / Convention de formation) executed in notarized or private form, filed electronically via LBR online filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; capital contributions are freely determined by the partnership agreement and may be in cash, in kind, or as an undertaking to contribute. No statutory escrow account is required for the SCSp under Luxembourg law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the founding partners desire to form an SCSp under Luxembourg law; RESOLVED that the partnership is constituted as a Special Limited Partnership, and the capital contributions set forth in the subscription schedule are accepted. RESOLVED that the exclusive registered office is fixed at 12, Rue de l'Eau, L-1449 Luxembourg, until relocated by the general partner. RESOLVED that the following officers are appointed: (a) Manager A as general partner and sole statutory manager, (b) Manager B as chief financial officer, and (c) Manager C as authorized signatory for bank and third-party matters. RESOLVED that the manager is instructed to file the partnership deed with the RCS, subscribe the entity to the UBO register, VAT number and social security registration, and take all acts to effect formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve and Verify Corporate Name in Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name availability search via RCS. File a name reservation application or incorporate directly using the registered corporate name stating the legal form SCSp. Ensure the name is not misleading, identical, or confusingly similar to an existing registered name.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of natural person filer
Draft partnership agreement showing proposed name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected, submit alternative name choices within 5 business days; the registry allows one free amendment to a rejected application before a new filing fee applies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Partnership Agreement and Governance Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or non-notarized private form; if a notary is used, submit to an approved Luxembourg notary office; alternatively registered through the RCS platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement in English, French, or German. Include SCSp specific clauses: name, registered office, general partner powers, limited partner information (including non-disclosure election), capital contribution schedule, profit allocation, and managers' authority. Execute by all partners; arrange notarization if using a deed of formation.
required_dossiers: Statement of contribution in cash or in kind
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or RCS reviewer identifies missing legal provisions, submit revised deed within 10 business days; no restart of filing prescribed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Deed with RCS and Publish Statutory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg Business Registers, with legal publication through the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed deed and completed application forms via the LBR online filing portal. Pay the required EUR 130-175 filing fee (or existing tariff). The registry issues the RCS certificate after validation. After registration, the deed is published in RESA to give third-party effect.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registered office acceptance from the lessor
Bank confirmation of capital contribution if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a cure request, provide the requested documentation within 15 days. If the filing is rejected, refile without prejudice, and if deadline is missed, apply for restoration of the original filing position with the district court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (UBO Register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Register of Beneficial Owners (UBO Register, managed by the Customs and Excise Administration under delegated authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, file the UBO declaration online stating all natural persons owning more than 25% of the partnership or controlling it through managerial authority. For SCSp, limited partners may be exempt from public filing if the partnership elects non-disclosure status. Retain documentary evidence of beneficial ownership.
required_dossiers: Proof of rights or exemptions for each UBO
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UBO filing is ambiguous, respond to the registry's warning to clarify ownership or provide evidence of exemption; non-compliance may trigger administrative fines but is curable before final assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Tax, Social Security, and VAT Identification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / LIR) for corporate income tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) for social security
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File VAT registration form (Formulaire 10B/10C) if taxable activities are performed; register for Luxembourg tax number (matricule) if not already automatic with RCS registration. Submit business opening declaration (déclaration d'activité) to the tax office. Register employer or self-employed status with CCSS if hiring personnel.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late VAT registration may result in penalties; file a voluntary regularization declaration with the AEDT. Tax number assignment is automatic upon RCS registration through the cross-office data exchange.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Luxembourg Bank Account and Complete KYC/AML Checks
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g., authorities acting under the CSSF supervision rules on anti-money laundering)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the formation dossier to a Luxembourg bank (such as an international bank with SICAV/private clients desk), including the SCSp deed, proof of RCS registration, UBO register proof, and business plan for international copyright licensing. Execute account signing mandate and authorize Swift Wire and Letter of Credit payment rails.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening forms and KYC questionnaire
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, provide org chart, licensing agreements, and financial projections. If the account is dormant, renew file after six months with updated practical ownership statement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg — Industry & Commerce Division (Ministère de l'Économie, Direction générale de l'industrie et du commerce)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — independent motion picture copyright distribution and intellectual property licensing require no operating industrial permit under Luxembourg legislation

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement — Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no physical infrastructure or waste generation; no EIA registration or report triggered because the activity is purely administrative and intellectual property commercialization
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — no wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste streams generated by an office-based copyright licensing operation of an SCSp.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — no production, storage, or manufacturing facility. For the registered office only, obtain the landlord's fire safety and structural load attestation, and register with the relevant municipal fire authority if the office building occupancy requires a permanent safety certificate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (portal: https://impotsdirects.public.lu). Indirect taxes (VAT, registration, stamp duties): Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) (portal: https://aedt.public.lu; e-filing platform: https://pfi.tax.lu). Business registry and central identification: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (portal: https://www.lbr.lu) and the national Single Window for formalities (portal: https://guichet.lu). Customs and excise: Administration des douanes et accises (portal: https://douanes.public.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Constitutional filing: the SCSp formation deed must be executed by a Luxembourg notary and filed with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through guichet.lu within one month of formation; the RCS allocates the registration number (B-number) and the 13-digit Luxembourg national identification number (numéro d'identification / matricule). Step 2 — VAT identification: an application for VAT registration (Formulaire 102) is filed with the AEDT via the RCS formalities or the e-filing channel; the AEDT assigns a Luxembourg VAT number in the format 'LU' followed by 8 digits, enabling the SCSp to invoice and file VAT returns as a distinct taxable person. Step 3 — Transparency declaration: the general partner (associé gérant) must file the annual corporate income tax return confirming the fiscally transparent status of the SCSp under Article 186bis L.I.R. and allocating the taxable result to each partner, with supporting statements. Step 4 — Non-resident partners: partners without a Luxembourg establishment must obtain a Luxembourg matricule where required and, if they carry on a Luxembourg taxable activity without a local establishment, appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) acceptable to the AEDT. Step 5 — Ongoing maintenance: changes of name, seat, general partner, or activity must be filed with the RCS and reflected in the AEDT master data within 15 days; final deregistration occurs upon the SCSp's liquidation certificate (clôture de liquidation).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default under Article 186bis(1) L.I.R. (Law of 4 December 1967, as amended): it is not itself subject to corporate income tax (IRC) or municipal business tax (IMT). Luxembourg-resident partners are taxed directly on their distributive share of SCSp income; non-resident partners are taxable only on Luxembourg-source income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg real estate. For VAT purposes, however, the SCSp is a separate taxable person and must hold its own LU VAT registration for supplies of film-licensing services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Election 1 — Article 186bis(2) L.I.R. opt-in: the SCSp may, by joint written declaration of all partners and under strictly defined legal conditions, irrevocably elect to be treated as a fully taxable opaque entity subject to IRC and IMT. Election 2 — Semi-transparent fund regime: an SCSp structured as a reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF), investment company in risk capital (SICAR), or specialised investment fund (SIF) may elect special fund-taxation rules instead of ordinary partnership taxation. Election 3 — VAT grouping: under Article 10(A) of the amended VAT law of 12 February 1979, the SCSp and its related Luxembourg entities may elect to form a single taxable person for VAT purposes (VAT group), simplifying intercompany invoicing. Election 4 — ATAD-2 hybrid-mismatch alignment: where a foreign partner's jurisdiction does not recognise the SCSp's fiscal transparency, the taxpayer must apply the EU Anti-Tax-Avoidance Directive 2017/952 hybrid-mismatch analysis (Law of 21 December 2017, as amended), including the dual-inclusion income set-off and structured-arrangement disallowance elections; no US-style check-the-box form exists, and classification is determined by law plus supporting filings on the general partner's annual CIT return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée), governed by the amended Law of 12 February 1979 implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover threshold (exclusive of VAT) under Article 57 of the VAT law for the small-business exemption; taxable persons whose turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 must register for Luxembourg VAT, while those below the threshold may register voluntarily. Distance sales of goods and electronically supplied services (including digital film-streaming) to Luxembourg non-taxable persons are subject to the special EU threshold of EUR 10,000 for cross-border supplies, above which the destination-state VAT applies. For B2B film-licensing services to EU customers, the reverse-charge mechanism applies and no Luxembourg VAT is due, although the supplier may still be required to file recapitulative statements (EU sales lists) and be VAT-registered if it also makes domestic taxable supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance, government-approval, or digital-stamping regime for private-sector invoices. E-invoicing is mandatory for B2G (public-sector) transactions since 1 July 2021 using structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, PEPPOL). Under the Law of 26 November 2024, domestic B2B e-invoicing is being phased in: large taxable persons must issue structured e-invoices from 1 January 2026, with full roll-out for all taxable persons by 1 January 2027, in alignment with the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) framework; structured data must conform to the European standard EN 16931. Cross-border EU supplies require electronic submission of recapitulative statements by the 15th day of the following month, and the AEDT performs risk-based post-audits using the VAT Information Exchange System (VIS) and e-FISCAL audit tools; there is no mandatory API-based clearance for each invoice, but machine-readable preservation for six years is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to: (1) exports of physical goods (master prints, film reels, promotional media) dispatched or transported to a destination outside the European Union, under Article 60 of the VAT law, provided export proof is obtained within 90 days of supply, extendable to 180 days with prior authorisation; and (2) film-licensing services supplied to non-EU customers, which under the B2B place-of-supply rule of Article 19(1) of the VAT law are located outside Luxembourg's territorial VAT scope and thus bear no Luxembourg VAT (functional 0%). Eligibility is evidenced by the customer's non-EU establishment (valid foreign VAT ID or equivalent), the executed licensing agreement, and the actual payment flow. Film licences to EU customers are taxable in the customer's member state under reverse charge; B2C licences to non-EU final consumers are outside Luxembourg VAT, while B2C digital supplies to EU consumers are taxable in the consumer's state and may be reported via the Luxembourg One-Stop-Shop (OSS) portal.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / Document Administratif Unique — DAU) for physical consignments of film prints, masters, or promotional materials
Bill of Lading, airway bill, or CMR consignment note evidencing outward transport from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union
Inward Remittance Certificate issued by the Luxembourg paying bank evidencing receipt of the foreign licence fee within the statutory period
Executed film-licensing agreement and territorial exploitation statements evidencing the non-EU place of supply and commercial substance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: In cases of unjustified zero-rating or failed export substantiation, the AEDT may reassess the supply at the standard 17% VAT rate plus default interest of 0.8% per month from the due date (Article 28 of the VAT collection rules). The VAT penalty regime (Articles 65–71 of the VAT law) imposes a fine of 10% of the evaded tax for non-intentional omissions, 100% for intentional evasion, and up to 200% in aggravated cases, with possible criminal prosecution and imprisonment of up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 200,000 for fraudulent export documentation. Where the documentary bundle or FX repatriation evidence is absent, the AEDT may apply a rebuttable presumption of a taxable domestic supply and extend the reassessment period from 5 to 7 years in cases of fraud; retrospective clawback of refunds is pursued against the SCSp and its general partner, with non-resident partners remaining severally liable for evaded Luxembourg VAT where the structure is found to be artificial or sham.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting as the national central bank within the Eurosystem and exercising delegated national competences alongside the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential supervision of credit institutions and payment institutions is vested in the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) under the Luxembourg Law of 5 April 1993 on the financial sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is a fully convertible reserve currency with no exchange-control restrictions applicable in Luxembourg. As an EU Member State, Luxembourg fully applies the free movement of capital and payments under Article 63 TFEU, Directive 88/361/EEC, and the associated CJEU jurisprudence. Both current account flows (royalties, license fees, profit remittances) and capital account flows (equity injections, partnership capital calls, liquidation distributions) are freely convertible and transferable without prior BCL or CSSF authorization. A Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) structured as a transparent partnership faces no convertibility hurdle; the sole practical frictions are commercial-bank documentary diligence, EU/EBA sanctions screening, and FATCA/CRS reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg maintains no statutory export proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline for foreign-currency receipts derived from motion picture licensing or any other export of services and intellectual property. Foreign currency balances (USD, GBP, INR, CNY, etc.) may be held indefinitely in resident accounts or converted at commercial market rates. The only compliance duty is the BCL's statistical Balance of Payments reporting captured by Luxembourg credit institutions for transactions above reporting thresholds; this is a statistical observation duty, not a surrender or conversion mandate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess / BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (receipt of licensing royalties and disbursement of profit participations)
Capital Escrow Account (investor commitments and capital calls)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account (dual-account structure)
Capital Escrow Account and fiduciary administration
Operational Account (trade settlement via documentary credits)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational royalty collections; Low for capital escrow and large balance sheet activity. Luxembourg-authorized EMIs and Payment Services Firms (PSFs) licensed by the CSSF under PSD2, as well as EU-passported EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Ebury, PPRO, Lemonway), can technically onboard the SCSp for inbound licensing collections and outbound royalty disbursements in EUR/USD with SWIFT and SEPA clearing. However, EMIs may not grant credit, cannot offer overdraft or treasury line facilities, and often decline complex partnership vehicles with non-resident beneficial owners. For a film licensing SCSp, incumbent Tier-1 credit institutions remain mandatory for escrow of investor capital and for documentary credit (Letter of Credit) trade finance; EMI rails should be limited to low-velocity operational receipts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requires physical board-appearance in Luxembourg; CSSF AML/CFT regulations (as aligned with EU Directive 2015/849 and CSSF Circular 18/698 as amended) permit remote video identification and qualified electronic signatures for entities presenting a low-to-standard AML risk profile. In practice, however, incumbent credit institutions frequently require at least one in-person meeting at the Luxembourg registered office or at a Luxbridge office with the authorised officer, the SCSp general partner (Gérant), or a person holding a valid power of attorney from the partnership. In-person attendance is usually waived where (i) the director/beneficial owner holds an EU/EEA passport, (ii) the SCSp has a registered agent or domiciliation provider subject to CSSF supervision, and (iii) video-identification is performed by a CSSF-authorised third-party provider. For non-EU resident ultimate beneficial owners, banks will generally impose an interview requirement, either physically in Luxembourg or via a recognised foreign correspondent bank relationship.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of the SCSp beneficial ownership: an SCSp is not a separate legal personality and benefits from an exemption against central filing of beneficial-ownership data under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019; the bank cannot independently verify who controls the partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Notarised SCSp constituent act and limited partnership agreement reflecting the exact identity of General Partner and each Limited Partner; (2) contractual cascade of UBO declarations signed by each natural person ultimately controlling any partner corporate entity; (3) certified copies of passports/ID cards for all UBOs; (4) register of partners and capital account statements certified by the domiciliation agent; (5) consent letter from the CSSF-registered registered agent confirming its AML duties under Luxembourg law.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and source of wealth for film licensing receivables: banks flag intangible-asset revenue as difficult to verify, especially where license fees are settled via multi-tier distribution sub-agents in emerging markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Executed film licensing agreements and chain-of-title documentation evidencing valid copyright ownership by the SCSp or its licensor; (2) ISAN (International Standard Audiovisual Number) registration certificate and European Audiovisual Observatory dossier; (3) distribution statements from sales agents or sub-distributors; (4) audited royalty statements and payment schedules; (5) bank reference letters from prior jurisdictions; (6) an independent IP valuation opinion where lump-sum licensing fees exceed EUR 1 million.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and embargo screening of counterparties: film territorial distribution licences often cover jurisdictions subject to EU/UN sanctions (Russia, Iran, Syria, North Korea, Belarus) or high-risk third countries (China, India, Nigeria, UAE, Turkey).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) An EU/UN sanctions screening report for all licensees and ultimate distribution end-beneficiaries produced by a recognised compliance provider; (2) a territorial exclusivity schedule expressly excluding sanctioned territories; (3) contractual warranty clauses requiring compliance with EU restrictive measures; (4) end-user undertakings and no-re-export clauses; (5) a sanctions counsel legal opinion confirming the absence of EU nexus for retained legacy distribution windows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic substance and tax-transparent partnership concerns: the SCSp may be mischaracterised by the bank's global AML desk as a conduit or shell entity, particularly where the general partner is another Luxembourg SPV or a foreign corporate service provider.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Evidence of real economic activity: dedicated management offices, business bank statements, executed licensing contracts, royalty flow reports, and payroll or outsourced management agreements; (2) substance memorandum from the registered agent and local counsel confirming compliance with Luxembourg substance expectations and OECD BEPS nexus requirements; (3) historical financial statements of the SCSp (where voluminous for accounting purposes) or intercompany accounting ledgers; (4) proof of a physical Luxembourg registered office with employed staff or contracted CSSF-licensed administration provider.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Variable capital and unlimited partner changes: SCSp partnership law allows unrestricted admission of new partners without notarial formalities and capital contributions in kind (including film IP). Banks view frequent partner changes and IP-in-kind contributions as high-risk for tracing ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (1) Complete register of partnership interests updated within 10 business days of any transfer; (2) notarised or electronically logged assignment/waiver deeds for each capital call; (3) an independent audit trail of film IP contributions supported by ISAN registrations and valuation reports; (4) an express contractual lock-in of the KYC package that any new partner must execute before the bank notifies a change in UBO status; (5) periodic (annual) refresh of CDD files at the bank's request.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Investor capital contributions are routed via SWIFT MT103 payments from the investor's bank to the SCSp's designated capital escrow account, cleared in TARGET2 where the remitting institution is euro-area resident or via correspondent/ nostro clearing for non-euro currencies. Compliant transmission requires: (i) ISO 20022 Purpose Code 'CAPC' (Capital Contribution) in field 70/77B or the equivalent structured remittance element; (ii) full legal name and LEI (if available) of the SCSp as payee; (iii) explicit reference to the capital call notice and partner identity to enable the bank's source-of-funds verification; (iv) where capital is injected in IP-in-kind (film copyrights), a parallel physical deed of contribution registered with the Luxembourg tax and trade registry should be referenced but no wire transfer is needed; (v) for subscription exceeding EUR 100,000, the bank will require a sworn source of wealth statement and certified investor passports. Royalty collections from foreign sub-distributors enter via MT103 with Purpose Code 'ROYL' (Royalties and License Fees) and should be accompanied by the relevant distribution report in the remittance narrative. All inbound transfers are subject to EBA 2015/01 funds transfer regulation datascreening (compliance with the 'travel rule' requiring originator and beneficiary information).
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlement of film acquisition costs, royalty participations, and profit-sharing payments is executed through (i) SWIFT MT103 for straight-through fiat disbursements to licensors, sub-distributors, and financial co-producers, carrying Purpose Code 'ROYL' for royalties or 'TRAD' for trade payments; (ii) SWIFT MT700 documentary Letters of Credit (Commercial LC) for milestone-based production and delivery financing, where the SCSp's Luxembourg bank issues an LC in favour of a production company or laboratory with the bill of lading, delivery receipt, and certificate of origin as required documents; (iii) TARGET2 via the BCL settlement account for euro disbursements between EU counterparties; and (iv) bank draft or internal transfer for intra-group cross-border profit allocation. All outbound payments must pass the bank's payment filtering against EU restrictive measures, and any disbursement to a non-EU financial intermediary in a high-risk jurisdiction requires the counterparty IBAN/SWIFT BIC and a documented underlying commercial invoice or distribution agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable vanilla foreign-exchange forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) with tenors up to 24 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex with a CSSF-regulated credit institution.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing emerging-market currencies such as INR, CNY, BRL, TRY, NGN and MXN, cash-settled in EUR, available from Luxembourg and London market makers without requiring an underlying local delivery account.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/GBP) for multi-year licensing revenue streams, structured as either EMIR-cleared transactions (subject to mandatory clearing thresholds at the EUR 8 billion gross notional level) or bilaterally collateralised swaps under a CSA.

FX options (EUR call/USD put and EUR put/USD call) for asymmetric protection on large one-off film catalogue sales, permitted without speculative restrictions when documented as a hedge of identified licensing receivables.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (financial statements), management report and any statutory audit report filed and published with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the annual accounts; approval must occur within six months of the fiscal year-end. For a calendar-year SCSp, the effective filing deadline is 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is subject to administrative fines; continued default may trigger formal demand procedures and eventual administrative strike-off (radiation) from the Luxembourg Business Registers, with potential liability of the managers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership information return (déclaration annuelle) for the transparent SCSp, reporting income allocated to partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year financial period, the return is due no later than 31 December of the following year unless an extension is granted by the competent tax office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in administrative fines, default interest at 0.6% per month on any resulting partner-level assessments, and criminal sanctions for intentional non-filing or false declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner (RBE) record update and continuing accuracy confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after any change in beneficial ownership or partnership interest transfers; no fixed annual renewal date is prescribed, but the registered data must remain accurate at all times.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance with the RBE update requirement carries administrative fines and criminal penalties; managers may be held personally liable for persistent inaccuracies or failure to file.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is mandatory when the SCSp meets at least two of the three large-undertaking criteria for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, or average workforce above 50 employees. Audit may also be required where all general partners are limited-liability entities or where the partnership belongs to a group required to produce consolidated financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2008 on annual accounts, as amended, transposing EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU; EU-endorsed IFRS is permitted for consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg law does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation. The manager must instead maintain continuous accuracy of the RBE filing and update it within one month of every change in beneficial ownership or partnership interest transfer. Such transfers require contemporaneous updating of the internal partners register and retention of the assignment document.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,000 - USD 4,500 per year for a Luxembourg registered office / corporate agent with basic secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if below mandatory audit thresholds; USD 8,000 - USD 22,000 per year for a statutory audit of an active licensing partnership when thresholds are exceeded

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% corporate income tax (CIT) on taxable income exceeding EUR 200,000; 15% on the first tranche up to EUR 175,000; 16% on EUR 175,001 to EUR 200,000. Add 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT and municipal business tax at 6.75% (Luxembourg City) to 10.43% (high-rate communes), yielding an approximate combined headline burden of 24.94% in Luxembourg City. The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default and therefore no entity-level CIT is levied; the distributive shares are taxed in the hands of the partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday is available to an SCSp. The Luxembourg IP box (art. 50bis LIR) grants an 80% exemption on qualifying IP income but is strictly limited to patents, supplementary protection certificates, plant variety rights, orphan drugs, and copyright-protected software; independent film copyright licensing rights do NOT qualify. Effective relief for a transparent SCSp materialises only at partner level: corporate partners may invoke the participation exemption on capital gains/dividends, and treaty-resident partners may claim DTA relief on their profit allocations.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward, no statutory year limit under art. 110 LIR); utilisation is restricted for tax years 2020 onwards such that carried-forward losses cannot offset more than 70% of the portion of taxable income exceeding EUR 17,500,000 per year.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 470 (Déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) lodged electronically via MyGuichet professional space of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory deadline: 31 March of the year following the fiscal year-end (calendar-year balance sheet date 31 December); the ACD administratively extends the filing window to 31 December of the following year without penalty for filers that request/provide the annual accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification: SCSp name, RCS number, matricule fiscal, registered seat, general partner identity, and fiscal classification confirmation as a transparent partnership.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate partners must provide a Luxembourg address for service, appoint a Luxembourg tax representative if they carry on a commercial activity, and quote their foreign tax identification number on the declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of Luxembourg GAAP accounts to taxable result; report the distributive taxable profit of the SCSp attributed to the corporate partner after elimination of internal allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign partners must attach the SCSp's annual accounts signed by the general partner and reconcile the share in accordance with Luxembourg tax rules, including transfer-pricing adjustments for film-licensing royalty flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - IP amortisation and royalty deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amortisation of acquired film catalogues and deduction of licence fees paid to right-owners; substantiated by the underlying distribution agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalty payments to a non-resident related licensor must be benchmarked at arm's length; the declaration must identify the licensor and include a TP documentation index to avoid recharacterisation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recoverable Luxembourg withholding tax, foreign tax credits, and advanced payments. The transparent SCSp does not itself suffer CIT, but corporate partners claim credits arising from the SCSp's activities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach approved Form 870 relief applications and the Tax Residence Certificate of the partner; a foreign tax credit for source-country tax withheld on film revenues is available only if treaty relief is not elected.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% increase of the tax due (minimum EUR 50) plus late-payment interest at 0.6% per month; continued default permits official ex officio assessment with additional penalty up to EUR 3,000, and intentional non-filing constitutes criminal tax fraud under art. 426 LIR, punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 500,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 830 - Election for taxation as a corporate entity (option pour l'assujettissement à l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed with the ACD via MyGuichet.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The election must be declared before the beginning of the first fiscal year for which it is to apply and no later than the statutory filing date of that fiscal year's first return; reversion to fiscal transparency thereafter requires prior ACD consent and is subject to anti-abuse review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Formal declaration that the SCSp irrevocably elects full CIT, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax treatment, converting its status from fiscally transparent to taxable company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must sign written consent; once elected, the SCSp becomes a Luxembourg tax resident subject to reporting on its worldwide film-licensing income, and distributions become dividends potentially subject to 15% dividend WHT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Contributions in kind and acquisition cost of film rights at the effective date of election, substantiated by valuation reports and purchase agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign partners contributing film catalogues must support the valuation with an independent appraisal; the ACD may challenge excessive step-up as an abuse of the election regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: A defective or late Form 830 is void, leaving the default transparency regime intact; distributions then remain partner-level allocations. Erroneous claims can be sanctioned under general procedural penalties of EUR 250 to EUR 3,000 and, in abuse cases, reassessment plus 10% surcharge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: VAT declaration (modèle 1022) lodged via MyGuichet TVA e-portal; the SCSp registers for Luxembourg VAT if it carries out taxable film-licensing or distribution services from Luxembourg.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by the 15th day of the month following the period end for monthly filers, or by the 15th day after the end of the quarter for quarterly filers; small taxpayers may file annually by 30 April of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Film licensing royalties and distribution revenues invoiced to Luxembourg customers at the standard Luxembourg VAT rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the licensee is a non-resident taxable dealer, the reverse-charge transfers the VAT obligation to the customer; the non-resident licensor should not charge Luxembourg VAT and must state this on the invoice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg VAT self-assessed on film-rights acquisition and production services received from non-resident or non-established suppliers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident licensor is relieved of Luxembourg VAT registration; the SCSp, as recipient, accounts for output and input VAT simultaneously and must retain the supplier contract and invoice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Recoverable VAT on local production services, legal fees, bank charges, and marketing costs attributable to taxable licensing revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident suppliers' invoices must contain their foreign VAT identification or a statement that reverse-charge applies; missing documentation causes disallowance of input VAT recovery.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing produces a 10% increase of the VAT due (minimum EUR 25 per return) and monthly interest at 0.6%; omission of reverse-charge VAT is treated as a serious VAT infringement punishable by fines up to EUR 5,000 per violation under the Luxembourg VAT enforcement provisions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax (plus 7% solidarity surcharge, resulting in an effective 16.05%) on dividends distributed by a Luxembourg taxable company. Critical SCSp nuance: the fiscally transparent SCSp does not suffer dividend WHT; profit distributions to partners are recharacterised as allocable partnership income. If the SCSp elects corporate taxation under Form 830, distributions become dividends subject to 15% WHT, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (minimum 10% holding, 12-month holding period) and to 5% or 0% under most Luxembourg income tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident beneficial owner must (1) obtain an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the residence state tax authority; (2) complete Luxembourg Form 870 (application for exemption or reduced withholding at source) and lodge it with the ACD before the payment date; (3) provide sworn beneficial-ownership statements and, where required, documentary evidence of the economic substance underlying the film-rights investment; (4) obtain annual revalidation of the approval. The paying SCSp must retain the approved Form 870 and TRC copies for at least 10 years; missing documentation triggers gross-basis 15% WHT and the ACD may reject retroactive refund claims beyond the statutory claim period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties and film-copyright licence fees: since 1 January 2024, Luxembourg levies a 10% statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties paid to non-residents; the tax is withheld at source by the Luxembourg payer, with exemption applied automatically to payments to EU resident companies and to DTA-resident beneficial owners under the relief procedure; applicable treaty rates vary, commonly 5% or 0% (e.g., Luxembourg-United States treaty allocates 0% royalty WHT). Interest: no Luxembourg statutory WHT on ordinary commercial debt interest paid to non-resident companies; 0% rate unless the debt instrument is recharacterised as equity under the abuse-of-law doctrine.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File: mandatory where the MNE group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds EUR 750 million (aligned with the Country-by-Country Report threshold). Local File: mandatory where the group's consolidated revenue equals or exceeds EUR 50 million and the Luxembourg entity's cross-border related-party transactions exceed the following category thresholds per fiscal year: EUR 250,000 for intellectual property / royalty / film-licence transactions; EUR 500,000 for service transactions; EUR 1,000,000 for financial transactions; EUR 5,000,000 for goods transactions. The film-licensing SCSp is accordingly captured by the EUR 250,000 IP transaction threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price) - preferred for film royalty rate benchmarking
